back: A period of wars, state-building and migration in southern Africa, about the 1810s-1830s ('the crushing'); Difaqane in Sotho-Tswana.
Age regiments of young men who served the king together.
Shaka's short stabbing spear, used in close combat.
Chest attacked head-on; horns encircled from the sides; loins waited in reserve.

front: Who led the Mthethwa and helped Shaka rise?
back: Dingiswayo (killed by Zwide of the Ndwandwe in about 1817-1818).

front: When and by whom was Shaka assassinated?
back: 1828, by his half-brothers Dingane and Mhlangana.
Land pressure, drought (Madlathule), trade at Delagoa Bay, rival states, Shaka's expansion, possibly slave and labour raiding.

front: Which Nguni leader crossed the Zambezi in 1835?
New states formed in the Mfecane period?
back: Zulu, Swazi, Sotho, Gaza and Ndebele.
The Zulu first-fruits ceremony, led by the king.
